nodes.title: Alternating Quantities: Peak, RMS & Mean Values
points: Alternating voltage: e = e₀ sin(ωt); Alternating current: i = i₀ sin(ωt ± ϕ).
Peak value (e₀, i₀): Maximum amplitude of alternating waveform.
Average (Mean) Value over half cycle: e_avg = (2/π) e₀ ≈ 0.637 e₀; i_avg = (2/π) i₀ ≈ 0.637 i₀. (Average over full cycle is strictly zero).
Root Mean Square (RMS / Virtual / Effective) Value: e_rms = e₀ / √2 ≈ 0.707 e₀; i_rms = i₀ / √2 ≈ 0.707 i₀.
AC meters (hot-wire meters) measure RMS values based on heating effect (H ∝ i²).
Household supply 230 V AC means V_rms = 230 V ⟹ Peak voltage V₀ = 230 × √2 ≈ 325 V (hence AC is more dangerous than DC of same voltage).
Form Factor: Ratio of RMS value to average value = V_rms / V_avg = π / (2√2) ≈ 1.11.

nodes.title: AC through Pure Resistor (R), Inductor (L) & Capacitor (C)
points: Pure Resistor: e = e₀ sin(ωt) ⟹ i = (e₀/R) sin(ωt). Current and voltage are IN PHASE (ϕ = 0°). Resistance R is independent of frequency.
Pure Inductor: e = e₀ sin(ωt) ⟹ i = (e₀/X_L) sin(ωt − π/2). Voltage LEADS current by π/2 rad (90°), or current lags voltage by π/2.
Pure Capacitor: e = e₀ sin(ωt) ⟹ i = (e₀/X_C) sin(ωt + π/2). Current LEADS voltage by π/2 rad (90°), or voltage lags current by π/2.
Phasor: A vector rotating anti-clockwise about origin with angular frequency ω representing an alternating quantity.

nodes.title: Inductive & Capacitive Reactance
points: Inductive Reactance (X_L): Opposition offered by pure inductor to AC flow: X_L = ω L = 2π f L. SI unit: Ohm (Ω).
Frequency dependence of X_L: X_L ∝ f. For direct current (DC, f = 0): X_L = 0 (inductor offers zero resistance to DC). Blocks high frequency AC.
Capacitive Reactance (X_C): Opposition offered by pure capacitor to AC flow: X_C = 1 / (ω C) = 1 / (2π f C). SI unit: Ohm (Ω).
Frequency dependence of X_C: X_C ∝ 1/f. For direct current (DC, f = 0): X_C = ∞ (capacitor completely BLOCKS DC). Passes high frequency AC.

nodes.title: Series LCR Circuit & Impedance
points: When R, L, and C are connected in series across alternating source e = e₀ sin(ωt): Current i is common to all components.
Total voltage phasor: e₀ = √[V_R² + (V_L − V_C)²] = i₀ √[R² + (X_L − X_C)²].
Impedance (Z): Total opposition of LCR circuit: Z = √[R² + (X_L − X_C)²] = √[R² + (ωL − 1/ωC)²]. SI unit: Ohm (Ω).
Phase angle ϕ: tanϕ = (X_L − X_C) / R.
Case 1: X_L > X_C (Inductive circuit): ϕ > 0, voltage leads current by ϕ.
Case 2: X_C > X_L (Capacitive circuit): ϕ < 0, current leads voltage by ϕ.
Case 3: X_L = X_C (Resistive resonance): ϕ = 0, voltage and current are in phase.

nodes.title: Series Resonance & Acceptor Circuit
points: Condition for Series Resonance: Inductive reactance equals capacitive reactance: X_L = X_C ⟹ ω_r L = 1 / (ω_r C).
Resonant angular frequency: ω_r = 1 / √(LC); Resonant linear frequency: f_r = 1 / [2π √(LC)].
Characteristics of Series Resonance:
(1) Impedance is MINIMUM and purely resistive: Z_min = R.
(2) Current is MAXIMUM: i_max = e₀ / R.
(3) Phase difference ϕ = 0; Power factor cosϕ = 1.
(4) Voltage across L and C cancel each other (V_L = V_C, but 180° out of phase).
Called an Acceptor Circuit because it admits maximum current at resonant frequency; used in radio tuning.

nodes.title: Parallel Resonance & Rejector Circuit
points: A parallel resonant circuit consists of an inductor L (with coil resistance R) in parallel with capacitor C across an AC source.
Resonant frequency (for small R): f_r = (1 / 2π) √[1/(LC) − R²/L²] ≈ 1 / [2π √(LC)].
Characteristics of Parallel Resonance:
(1) Admittance is minimum ⟹ Impedance is MAXIMUM: Z_max = L / (CR).
(2) Current drawn from the source is MINIMUM: i_min = e₀ / Z_max.
(3) Circuit is purely resistive at resonance (cosϕ = 1).
Called a Rejector Circuit because it chokes/rejects current at resonant frequency; used in filter networks.

nodes.title: Power in AC Circuit, Power Factor & Wattless Current
points: Instantaneous power: p = e × i.
Average Power (True Power): P_avg = e_rms × i_rms × cosϕ. SI unit: Watt (W).
Apparent Power (Virtual Power): P_app = e_rms × i_rms. SI unit: Volt-Ampere (VA).
Power Factor: cosϕ = True Power / Apparent Power = R / Z.
In Pure Resistor: ϕ = 0 ⟹ cosϕ = 1 ⟹ P_avg = e_rms i_rms (maximum power dissipation).
In Pure Inductor or Capacitor: ϕ = π/2 ⟹ cosϕ = 0 ⟹ P_avg = 0 (no power consumed).
Wattless Current (Idle Current): Component of current that consumes zero power: i_w = i_rms sinϕ.

nodes.title: Sharpness of Resonance & Quality Factor (Q-Factor)
points: Sharpness of resonance indicates how rapidly current falls off on either side of resonant frequency f_r.
Bandwidth: Δf = f₂ − f₁ = R / (2π L), where f₁ and f₂ are half-power frequencies (where power is half max and current is i_max / √2).
Quality Factor (Q-Factor): Measure of sharpness and voltage magnification: Q = f_r / Δf = ω_r L / R = 1 / (ω_r C R) = (1/R) √(L/C).
Higher Q-factor means sharper resonance, smaller bandwidth, and better tuning selectivity (desirable in receivers).
Smaller resistance R gives higher Q-factor and sharper peak.

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Derivations & Transformers
points: Board Favourite #1: Derive expression for impedance Z and phase angle ϕ of a series LCR AC circuit using phasor diagram.
Board Favourite #2: Obtain expression for resonant frequency of series LCR circuit and state conditions for resonance.
Board Favourite #3: Derive average power dissipated in AC circuit P_avg = e_rms i_rms cosϕ and explain wattless current.
Board Favourite #4: Explain principle, construction, and working of a Transformer with neat diagram.
Transformer Formula: Transformation ratio K = N_s / N_p = e_s / e_p = i_p / i_s.
Step-up Transformer: K > 1 (N_s > N_p, e_s > e_p, i_s < i_p); Step-down Transformer: K < 1 (N_s < N_p, e_s < e_p, i_s > i_p).
Efficiency of transformer: η = (Power output / Power input) × 100% = (e_s i_s / e_p i_p) × 100%.

nodes.title: MHT-CET Shortcuts, 'CIVIL' Mnemonic & Traps
points: Memory Mnemonic 'CIVIL': In Capacitor C, current I leads voltage V; In Inductor L, voltage V leads current I.

Choke Coil Shortcut: An inductor of high inductance L and negligible resistance R used to control AC current with minimum power wastage (P_avg ≈ 0 since cosϕ ≈ 0). Iron core choke used for low audio frequencies; air core for high radio frequencies.
Resonance Shift Trap: If both L and C are doubled, resonant frequency f_r is HALVED (f_r ∝ 1/√(LC)). If L is doubled and C is halved, f_r remains UNCHANGED.
Voltage across L and C Trap: At series resonance, V_L and V_C can individually be MUCH GREATER than the source voltage V_S by factor Q (Voltage Magnification = Q × V_S).
Transformer Trap: Transformers work ONLY on AC. On steady DC, flux change is zero (dΦ/dt = 0), so secondary voltage is strictly ZERO.

formulas.label: CIVIL phase rule
formulas.expr: C: I leads V | L: V leads I
